title: Stroke, Seizures and Syncope: The PCP's Calls

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already run FAST, check glucose, give oxygen, protect a seizing patient and transport fast. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Tell ischemic from hemorrhagic stroke, and why the clock rules
  2. Know what the PCP adds in the BC stroke protocol
  3. Manage seizures, TIA and syncope within BC scope

Textbook: Chapter 31, PDF pages 2856–2894
slides.say: Welcome back. Last lesson covered the brain's needs and the neuro exam; today we apply them to the big calls. As EMRs, you already run a FAST check, check the sugar, give oxygen, protect a seizing patient, and transport quickly. As a PCP, you'll make more decisions on these calls, and you'll start IVs on stroke patients under very specific rules. Today we'll cover three things: the two kinds of stroke and why the clock rules everything, what the PCP adds in the BC stroke protocol, and how to handle seizures, TIAs and fainting within BC scope.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。上节课讲了大脑的需求和神经系统检查，今天把它们用到几类重要的出诊上。作为 EMR，你们已经会做 FAST 检查、测血糖、给氧、保护抽搐的病人、快速转运。作为 PCP，这些出诊里你要做更多判断，还要按非常具体的规则给卒中病人开静脉。今天讲三件事：两类卒中，以及为什么时间决定一切；BC 卒中流程里 PCP 多做什么；以及在 BC 范围内怎么处理癫痫发作、TIA 和晕厥。

slides.title: Ischemic, hemorrhagic, or TIA
slides.body:
TIAbrief loss of blood flowsigns clear within hours
Ischemica clot blocks a vesselabout 4 in 5 strokes; deficits plateau
Hemorrhagicbleeding inside the skullkeeps worsening; ICP rises
  • "Worst headache of my life" → think bleed
  • Most patients are over 65; atrial fibrillation raises the risk
slides.say: A stroke, or CVA, means part of the brain loses its blood supply. About four in five strokes are ischemic: a clot blocks a vessel, and the deficits usually level off. A hemorrhagic stroke is a bleed inside the skull; it tends to keep getting worse as the ICP rises. The classic clue is the worst headache of the patient's life, then trouble speaking and a falling level of consciousness. A TIA, or transient ischemic attack, looks like a stroke but clears within hours. Most stroke patients are over sixty-five, and atrial fibrillation is a big risk, because clots form in the heart.
slides.sayZh: 卒中也叫 CVA，是部分大脑失去血液供应。大约五分之四的卒中是缺血性的：血栓堵住血管，症状通常到一定程度就停在平台期。出血性卒中是颅内出血，随着颅内压升高往往越来越重。典型线索是病人说这是一生中最痛的头痛，随后说话困难、意识下降。TIA，即短暂性脑缺血发作，看起来像卒中，但几小时内就消退。多数卒中病人超过六十五岁，房颤是重要危险因素，因为血栓会在心脏里形成。

slides.title: Time is brain
slides.body:
Clot-busting drugs: within 4.5 hours of onset

  • Large-vessel clots: clot removal, also time-critical
  • Key fact: when was the patient last known normal?
  • Woke up with symptoms → clock starts when last seen well
  • Bring a family member or witness if you can
  • Document: last normal, onset, changes en route, hospital choice
slides.say: Why the rush? For an ischemic stroke, the hospital's clot-busting drugs, called fibrinolytics, must be given within four and a half hours of onset. Pulling out a large clot also works best early. So the most important fact you collect is when the patient was last known normal. If they live alone, ask family or caregivers. If they woke up with symptoms, the clock starts when they were last seen well, not when they woke. Bring a family member or witness if you can. Document the last normal time, the onset, any change en route, and why you chose that hospital.
slides.sayZh: 为什么要这么急？缺血性卒中，医院的溶栓药必须在发病后四个半小时内给；取出大血栓也是越早越好。所以你要收集的最重要信息，是病人最后一次被确认正常的时间。独居的病人，问家属或照护者。如果病人醒来时就有症状，时间要从最后一次被看到正常时算起，而不是醒来的时间。能带家属或目击者同行就带上。记录最后正常时间、发病时间、途中变化，以及你为什么选这家医院。

slides.title: Stroke screening tools
slides.body:
ToolChecksMeaning
CPSSface, arm drift (10 s), speechany abnormal: 72%
LAPSSage, history, glucose, one-sided weaknessall criteria met: 97%
FAST-VAN (BC)after FAST: vision, aphasia, neglectsuggests a large-vessel stroke

Neither arm moves? The patient may not have understood. Repeat it.
slides.say: The book shows several screening tools. The Cincinnati scale, or CPSS, checks facial droop, arm drift with eyes closed and palms up for ten seconds, and speech. If any one is abnormal, the chance of stroke is about seventy-two percent. The Los Angeles screen, LAPSS, adds age, history, blood sugar and one-sided weakness; when every item is met, it's about ninety-seven percent. The BC protocol names FAST-VAN. After a positive FAST, check V, A, N: vision problems, aphasia, and neglect, which means the patient ignores one side. A positive VAN suggests a large-vessel blockage, the kind that may need clot removal.
slides.sayZh: 书里介绍了几种筛查工具。辛辛那提量表 CPSS 查面部下垂、闭眼掌心向上平举双臂十秒看是否漂移，以及言语。任何一项异常，卒中的可能性约百分之七十二。洛杉矶筛查 LAPSS 加上年龄、病史、血糖和单侧无力，全部符合时约百分之九十七。BC 流程用的是 FAST-VAN：FAST 阳性后再查 V、A、N，也就是视觉问题、失语和忽视，忽视是指病人对一侧视而不见。VAN 阳性提示大血管堵塞，这类卒中可能需要取栓。

slides.q: At 07:30, a man finds his wife confused with right arm weakness. She went to bed normal at 22:00 and woke like this at 06:45. What onset time do you report?
options: 22:00, when she was last known normal
Unknown, so the time doesn't matter
slides.say: Let's pause for a question. At seven thirty in the morning, a man finds his wife confused, with weakness in her right arm. She went to bed normal at ten p.m. and woke up like this at six forty-five. What onset time do you report? A, six forty-five, when she woke up. B, seven thirty, when she was found. C, ten p.m., when she was last known normal. D, unknown, so the time doesn't matter. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 停一下考考你：早上七点半，一位男士发现妻子意识混乱、右臂无力。她前一晚十点上床时一切正常，早上六点四十五醒来就是这样。你报告的发病时间是哪个？A 六点四十五，她醒来时；B 七点半，被发现时；C 晚上十点，最后确认正常时；D 不清楚，所以时间不重要。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is C, ten p.m. Onset is the time the patient was last known normal. She may have had the stroke at any point during the night, so the clock starts when she was last seen well. A and B would make the stroke look more recent than it may be, which could lead to unsafe treatment. D is wrong: the time always matters, because it decides which treatments are still possible.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 C，晚上十点。发病时间按最后确认正常的时间算。她可能在夜里任何时候发生卒中，所以要从最后一次被看到正常时开始计时。A 和 B 会让卒中看起来比实际更近，可能导致不安全的治疗。D 错，时间永远重要，它决定哪些治疗还来得及。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: the BC stroke protocol
slides.body:
Use for any neuro deficit, altered LOC, airway trouble, abnormal breathing, or a weak, rapid or absent radial pulse.

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Assess and manage ABCs
  • O₂ to SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  • Position the patient
  • Blood glucose check
  • Accurate recognition: FAST-VAN
  • Timely transport; notify the hospital en route

PCP adds (en route)

  • Vascular access
  • Size 18 G
  • Site above the wrist
  • Preferably the right side
slides.say: Here's the BC stroke protocol. You use it for any neurological deficit, an altered level of consciousness, trouble keeping the airway, abnormal breathing, or a weak, rapid or absent radial pulse. The left column is familiar from EMR practice: ABCs, oxygen to ninety-four percent or more, positioning, a glucose check, recognition with FAST-VAN, and timely transport while you notify the hospital. The PCP adds one thing, and it's very specific: vascular access, en route, with an eighteen gauge catheter, at a site above the wrist, preferably on the right side. Notice the words en route. The IV never holds you on scene.
slides.sayZh: 这是 BC 卒中流程。适用于任何神经功能缺损、意识改变、难以维持气道、呼吸异常，或桡动脉搏动弱、快或摸不到的病人。左栏你作为 EMR 都很熟悉：ABC、给氧到九十四以上、摆体位、测血糖、用 FAST-VAN 准确识别、及时转运并通知医院。PCP 只多一件事，而且非常具体：在转运途中建立静脉通路，用十八号针，部位在手腕以上，最好在右侧。注意「途中」两个字：开静脉绝不能让你滞留现场。

slides.title: The stroke call, start to finish
slides.body:
ABCs, O₂, glucose→FAST-VAN, last normal→go + notify→IV en route
  • Protect the airway; suction ready
  • Protect numb or weak limbs from injury
  • No aspirin: it can harm a bleeding stroke
  • High BP: no standard prehospital treatment
  • Repeat FAST-VAN and GCS en route
slides.say: Let's put the call together. ABCs, oxygen, and a sugar check first, because a low sugar can look exactly like a stroke. Then FAST-VAN and the last-known-normal time. Then go, and call ahead so the stroke team is ready; your IV happens in the ambulance. On the way, keep suction ready and protect the airway. Protect a numb or weak limb, because the patient can't feel it getting hurt. Don't give aspirin, because a bleeding stroke can get worse. The book says there's no standard prehospital treatment for the high blood pressure. Repeat your stroke screen and GCS, and record any change.
slides.sayZh: 把整个出诊串起来。先 ABC、给氧、测血糖，因为低血糖可以和卒中一模一样。然后做 FAST-VAN，确定最后正常时间。接着出发，提前通知，让卒中团队做好准备；静脉在救护车上开。途中备好吸引、保护气道。保护麻木或无力的肢体，因为病人感觉不到它受伤。不要给阿司匹林，出血性卒中会因此加重。书里说，院前对高血压没有标准处理。途中要重复卒中筛查和 GCS，并记录任何变化。

slides.title: TIA and stroke look-alikes
slides.body:
• TIA: stroke signs that clear within hours
  • More than 1 in 3 TIA patients have a stroke soon after
  • Treat a TIA like a stroke; strongly urge transport
  • Look-alikes: low sugar, postictal confusion, Bell palsy
  • Bell palsy: sudden one-sided face droop; unsure → treat as stroke
slides.say: Sometimes you arrive and the patient looks perfectly normal. That may be a TIA: stroke signs that cleared within hours, with no lasting damage. Don't relax. More than one in three of these patients will have a stroke soon after, so treat it like a stroke, reassess often, and strongly encourage transport; ask family to help if the patient refuses. Also know the look-alikes. A low sugar can cause weakness and confusion. After a seizure, a patient can be confused and unable to speak for a while. And Bell palsy, a sudden paralysis of the facial nerve, causes a one-sided facial droop. The book's rule: if you're not sure, treat it as a stroke.
slides.sayZh: 有时你到场时病人看起来完全正常，这可能是 TIA：卒中症状在几小时内消退，不留永久损伤。别放松。超过三分之一的 TIA 病人不久后会发生卒中，所以按卒中处理，勤复评，并强烈劝其转运；病人拒绝时请家属帮忙。还要认识「冒充者」：低血糖会引起无力和意识混乱；癫痫发作后，病人可能一段时间内意识混乱、说不出话；Bell 麻痹是面神经突然麻痹，会造成一侧面瘫。书里的原则是：拿不准，就按卒中处理。

slides.title: Altered LOC: think AEIOU-TIPS
slides.body:
AEIOUTIPS
Alcohol, acidosisTrauma
EpilepsyInfection
InsulinPsychosis
OverdoseStroke
Uremia—

A smell of alcohol isn't the whole story. Ask: last normal, all meds, how fast it began.
slides.say: When the cause of an altered level of consciousness isn't obvious, use AEIOU-TIPS: alcohol or acidosis, epilepsy, insulin, overdose, uremia, then trauma, infection, psychosis, and stroke. Uremia means waste building up when the kidneys fail. A patient who smells of alcohol can still be in a coma from something else, like a low sugar or a head injury. Ask when the patient was last normal, and how fast it came on: infections rarely cause coma in an instant, but seizures can. Check every medication, including herbal products and street drugs. Older adults often take many drugs, and the combinations can affect the brain.
slides.sayZh: 意识改变原因不明时，用 AEIOU-TIPS 口诀：酒精或酸中毒、癫痫、胰岛素、过量、尿毒症，再加外伤、感染、精神疾病和卒中。尿毒症是肾衰竭时废物在体内蓄积。有酒味的病人，昏迷仍可能另有原因，比如低血糖或头部外伤。要问最后正常是什么时候、起病有多快：感染很少瞬间导致昏迷，而癫痫发作可以。查清所有药物，包括草药和毒品。老年人常同时服很多药，药物组合可能影响大脑。

slides.title: Seizure types
slides.body:
TypeWhat you see
Tonic-clonicaura → LOC → stiffening → jerking → postictal
Absencea child stops and stares for seconds; no postictal
Simple partialone body part jerks or tingles
Complex partialaltered awareness, small odd movements
Pseudoseizurelooks real, psychological cause: treat as real
slides.say: A seizure is a sudden, disorganized firing of neurons. The generalized tonic-clonic seizure is the one you know: often an aura first, like a strange taste or flashing lights, then loss of consciousness, stiffening, and rhythmic jerking. Then comes the postictal phase, when the brain resets. It can last minutes to hours, with confusion, sleepiness, headache, or trouble speaking. Absence seizures are mostly in children: they stop and stare for a few seconds, with no postictal phase. Partial seizures involve one area of the brain: simple partial means one body part jerks or tingles; complex partial changes awareness. A pseudoseizure has a psychological cause, but you still treat it as a seizure.
slides.sayZh: 癫痫发作是神经元突然、无序地放电。全面性强直阵挛发作你们都见过：常先有先兆，比如嘴里有怪味或看到闪光，然后意识丧失、全身僵直、节律性抽动。接着是发作后期，大脑在「重启」，可持续几分钟到几小时，表现为意识混乱、嗜睡、头痛或说不出话。失神发作多见于儿童：停住发呆几秒，没有发作后期。部分性发作只涉及大脑一个区域：简单部分性是身体某一部位抽动或发麻，复杂部分性会改变意识状态。假性发作源于心理因素，但你仍然要按癫痫发作处理。

slides.title: Managing a seizure
slides.body:
• Protect from injury; don't restrain; nothing in the mouth
  • Not breathing for over 30 seconds → ventilate
  • Check glucose; correct a low (PCP: D10W)
  • Status epilepticus: over 4–5 min, or no waking between seizures
  • Book's drugs (benzodiazepines): not on the BC licensing exam
  • So: airway, BVM, O₂, glucose, rapid transport, notify
slides.say: During a seizure, your job is protection. Move hard objects away, pad the area, and don't restrain the patient or put anything in the mouth; if a bystander placed a spoon there, take it out. Short pauses in breathing are common, but if the patient stops breathing for more than thirty seconds, start ventilating. Check the sugar, and as a PCP, correct a low with D10W. Status epilepticus means a seizure lasting more than four to five minutes, or seizures back to back without waking in between. It can kill. The book's drugs for it, benzodiazepines, aren't on the BC licensing exam. So your plan is airway, bag-valve mask and oxygen, glucose, rapid transport, and an early call to the hospital.
slides.sayZh: 发作过程中，你的任务是保护。移开硬物、垫好周围，不要约束病人，也不要往嘴里放任何东西；如果旁人塞了勺子，把它取出来。短暂的呼吸停顿很常见，但如果停止呼吸超过三十秒，就要开始通气。测血糖，作为 PCP，低血糖就用 D10W 纠正。癫痫持续状态是指一次发作超过四到五分钟，或者连续发作、中间没有清醒过。它可以致命。书里用来止抽的苯二氮卓类执照考试不考。所以你的方案是：气道、球囊面罩和给氧、血糖、快速转运，并尽早通知医院。

slides.q: You're a PCP. A 30-year-old has seized for 7 minutes and hasn't woken between two seizures. BGL is 6.2 mmol/L. Which plan fits the BC protocols?
options: Hold the limbs still to prevent injury
Protect, support the airway, ventilate as needed, transport fast, notify
Wait on scene until the seizure stops
slides.say: Now a PCP decision. You're a PCP. A thirty-year-old has been seizing for seven minutes and hasn't woken between two seizures. The blood sugar is six point two. Which plan fits the BC protocols? A, give midazolam IM, then transport. B, hold the limbs still to prevent injury. C, protect the patient, support the airway, ventilate as needed, transport fast, and notify the hospital. D, wait on scene until the seizure stops. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。你是 PCP，一位三十岁的病人已经抽搐七分钟，两次发作之间没有醒过，血糖六点二。哪个方案符合 BC 流程？A 肌注咪达唑仑，然后转运；B 按住四肢以防受伤；C 保护病人、支持气道、需要时通气、快速转运并通知医院；D 在现场等发作停止。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is C. This is status epilepticus, a true emergency. The sugar is normal, so D10W isn't indicated. Under the BC protocols, you protect the patient, support the airway and ventilate if needed, and move fast while you call ahead. A is the book's treatment, but benzodiazepines aren't on the BC licensing exam. B is wrong because you never restrain seizing limbs. D wastes time: a seizure that has lasted this long may not stop on its own.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 C。这是癫痫持续状态，真正的急症。血糖正常，所以不需要 D10W。按 BC 流程，你要保护病人、支持气道、需要时通气，并一边通知医院一边快速转运。A 是书里的处理，但苯二氮卓类执照考试不考。B 错，绝不能约束抽搐的肢体。D 浪费时间：持续这么久的发作可能不会自己停。

slides.title: Stroke, seizure or syncope?
slides.body:
StrokeSeizureSyncope
Beforemaybe headacheauradizzy, vision changes
Duringone-sided weaknesswhole-body movementlimp; usually standing
Aftermay clear, stay or worsenslow to reorientquick to reorient

Fainting is over in under 60 s. Older adult: think heart rhythm. Transport all unexplained cases.
slides.say: These three are easy to mix up, so compare them. Before the event, a stroke may start with a headache, a seizure often has an aura, and syncope, or fainting, comes with dizziness, weakness or vision changes, usually while standing. During it, a stroke gives one-sided weakness, a seizure gives whole-body movement that usually stops within one to two minutes, and a fainting patient lies limp. Afterward, seizure patients are slow to reorient, fainting patients recover quickly, and stroke signs may clear, stay, or worsen. Fainting is over in under a minute. In older adults it's often a heart rhythm problem, so look for cardiac causes, check the sugar and any fall injuries, and transport.
slides.sayZh: 这三种很容易混淆，对比着记。事前：卒中可能先有头痛，癫痫发作常有先兆，晕厥则伴头晕、乏力或视物改变，通常发生在站立时。事中：卒中是单侧无力，癫痫是全身性动作，通常一到两分钟内停止，晕厥的病人是瘫软的。事后：癫痫病人定向力恢复慢，晕厥的病人很快恢复，卒中症状可能消退、不变或加重。晕厥一分钟内就结束。老年人晕厥常是心律问题，所以要查心源性原因、测血糖、查摔伤，并转运。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• The stroke IV is en route: never delay transport for it
  • 18 G, above the wrist, right side preferred
  • No ASA for stroke: in BC it's for cardiac chest pain
  • D10W for a confirmed low only: high sugar can worsen a stroke
  • Status epilepticus: no BC exam drug stops it, so move fast
  • Seat patients before you start an IV: needles cause fainting
slides.say: Here are the pitfalls that are new at PCP level. First, the stroke IV belongs in the ambulance; starting it on scene costs brain time. Second, follow the protocol's details: eighteen gauge, above the wrist, right side preferred. Third, you'll give aspirin often for chest pain, so it's easy to reach for it here. Don't. In BC, ASA is for cardiac chest pain, and a stroke may be a bleed. Fourth, give D10W only for a confirmed low, because high sugar can worsen stroke damage. Fifth, in status epilepticus, no drug on the BC licensing exam will stop it, so speed is your treatment. And sit your patient down before you start an IV; needles are a classic trigger for fainting.
slides.sayZh: 下面是 PCP 层级才会遇到的陷阱。第一，卒中的静脉在救护车上开，在现场开会耗掉大脑的时间。第二，照流程细节做：十八号针、手腕以上、最好右侧。第三，胸痛时你会经常给阿司匹林，所以这里很容易顺手去拿。别给。在 BC，ASA 是用于心源性胸痛的，而卒中可能是出血。第四，D10W 只给确认的低血糖，因为高血糖会加重卒中损伤。第五，癫痫持续状态在执照考试的药里没有能止住的，速度就是你的治疗。还有，开静脉前先让病人坐下，针头是诱发晕厥的经典原因。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Book: CPSS, LAPSS, Ontario card → BC protocol: FAST-VAN
  • Book: SpO₂ 94–99% → BC: ≥ 94%
  • Benzodiazepines for seizures: not on the BC exam
  • Book: D50W → BC: D10W (PCP) for BGL < 4.0
  • Headache: morphine, meperidine, ketorolac → not on the BC exam (BCEHS added scope: morphine, ketorolac)
  • Stroke IV: 18 G, above the wrist, right side, en route
slides.say: Let's compare the book with BC. The book teaches the Cincinnati scale, the Los Angeles screen, and an Ontario prompt card; the BC protocol names FAST-VAN. The book titrates oxygen to ninety-four to ninety-nine percent; BC says ninety-four percent or higher. For seizures the book uses benzodiazepines, which aren't on the BC licensing exam. The book's sugar drug is D50W; in BC, the PCP gives D10W for a blood sugar under four point oh. For headache, the book lists morphine, meperidine and ketorolac, and none of them are on the BC exam drug list, though BCEHS PCPs may give morphine or ketorolac after added-scope training. And memorize the BC stroke IV: eighteen gauge, above the wrist, preferably right side, started en route.
slides.sayZh: 把书和 BC 比一比。书里教辛辛那提量表、洛杉矶筛查和安大略提示卡；BC 流程用的是 FAST-VAN。书里给氧目标是百分之九十四到九十九；BC 是九十四以上。癫痫发作书里用苯二氮卓类，执照考试不考。书里的补糖药是 D50W；在 BC，血糖低于四点零时 PCP 给 D10W。头痛时书里列了吗啡、哌替啶和酮咯酸，都不在 BC 考试药物清单上；BCEHS 的 PCP 经扩展范围（Schedule 1/2）培训后可以用吗啡或酮咯酸。还要背熟 BC 卒中静脉：十八号针、手腕以上、最好右侧、途中开。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Get the last-known-normal time; clot-busters within 4.5 h
  2. PCP adds an 18 G IV, above the wrist, right side, en route
  3. Seizures: protect, ventilate, glucose; no benzos on the BC exam, so move fast

Next: Chapter 32, Endocrine Emergencies
slides.say: Let's wrap up with three things to remember. One: the key fact on every stroke call is the time the patient was last known normal, because clot-busting drugs only work within four and a half hours. Two: the BC stroke protocol is FAST-VAN, notify, and go, and the PCP adds an eighteen gauge IV above the wrist, preferably on the right, started en route, never at the cost of scene time. Three: for seizures, protect the patient, ventilate if needed, and check the sugar; with no benzodiazepines on the BC exam, rapid transport is your treatment for status epilepticus. Next chapter: endocrine emergencies. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，每次卒中出诊最关键的信息是最后确认正常的时间，因为溶栓药只在四个半小时内有效。二，BC 卒中流程是 FAST-VAN、通知、出发；PCP 多一条十八号、手腕以上、最好右侧的静脉，在途中开，绝不为它耽误现场时间。三，癫痫发作要保护病人、必要时通气、测血糖；执照考试里没有苯二氮卓类，所以对癫痫持续状态，快速转运就是你的治疗。下一章讲内分泌急症。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
